D.t: Brian Bengs trails by 15.7 and wins 2% of simulations. Closing it takes about 30,045 voters switching sides, or 60,091 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +24.0 and R +6.4. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +11.5. Your best recent poll is Concord Public Opinion Partners (D) at R +1.8; your worst is Quantus Insights at R +19.0. 6 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Minnehaha, a projected net 6,532 votes; Oglala Lakota, a projected net 2,807 votes; Todd, a projected net 1,572 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Minnehaha, D +7.9, 21.6% of the vote; Brookings, R +3.0, 3.6% of the vote; Yankton, R +12.0, 2.6% of the vote; Roberts, R +0.9, 1.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Brian Bengs runs furthest behind in Hughes, Butte, Meade. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 91% of voters, 41 to 59, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.57 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 74% of voters, 42 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.69 points; Voters without a degree, 64% of voters, 42 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.18 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Brian Bengs: Immigration voters 10 to 90, Voters who can afford daily costs 30 to 70, Incomes $125K and up 35 to 65. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$51K cash against $2.7M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Registered Democrats cast 30% of the 49,438 ballots in South Dakota so far, against 53% for the other party. That is 3.9 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 1.7 points away from Brian Bengs. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Air cover: Outside groups spent $1.4M helping Mike Rounds and $0 helping Brian Bengs.

R.t: Mike Rounds leads by 15.7 in the forecast and wins 98% of simulations. The cushion is about 60,091 votes; a one point swing is about 1,919 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +6.4 and R +24.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +11.5. Your best recent poll is Quantus Insights at R +19.0; your worst is Concord Public Opinion Partners (D) at R +1.8. 6 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Pennington, a projected net 6,212 votes; Meade, a projected net 5,714 votes; Lincoln, a projected net 4,473 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Minnehaha, D +7.9, 21.6% of the vote; Brookings, R +3.0, 3.6% of the vote; Yankton, R +12.0, 2.6% of the vote; Roberts, R +0.9, 1.0% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Mike Rounds runs furthest behind in Minnehaha, Clay. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 91% of voters, 59 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.57 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 74% of voters, 58 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.69 points; Voters without a degree, 64% of voters, 58 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.18 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Mike Rounds: Independents 28 to 72, Health care and Social Security voters 32 to 68, Asian and other voters 34 to 66. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.7M cash against $51K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
